description: Design a 3-to-8 decoder in Verilog. The decoder should have 3 input lines (A2, A1, A0) and 8 output lines (Y7 to Y0). description: Design a restoring divider in Verilog that takes a 4-bit dividend and a 4-bit divisor as inputs and produces a 4-bit quotient and a 4-bit remainder as outputs. The divider should be able to handle cases where the divisor is zero by setting the quotient and remainder to zero. The operation should be clocked, and the division process should occur over several clock cycles.
code:
module restoring_divider(
    input clk,
    input rst,
    input start,
    input [3:0] dividend,
    input [3:0] divisor,
    output reg [3:0] quotient,
    output reg [3:0] remainder,
    output reg done
);
    reg [3:0] A; // Accumulator
    reg [3:0] Q; // Quotient
    reg [4:0] D; // Divisor with one bit extension for subtraction
    reg [2:0] count; // Count for cycle
    reg state; // State machine

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            A <= 0;
            Q <= 0;
            remainder <= 0;
            quotient <= 0;
            done <= 0;
            count <= 0;
            state <= 0;
        end else begin
            case (state)
                0: begin // Initialization
                    if (start) begin
                        A <= dividend;
                        Q <= 0;
                        D <= {1'b0, divisor}; // Extend divisor
                        count <= 4; // Set count for 4 cycles
                        state <= 1; // Move to next state
                        done <= 0;
                    end
                end
                1: begin // Division process
                    if (count > 0) begin
                        A <= {A[2:0], Q[3]}; // Shift left
                        if (A >= D[3:0]) begin
                            A <= A - D[3:0]; // Subtract divisor
                            Q <= {Q[2:0], 1'b1}; // Set bit in quotient
                        end else begin
                            Q <= {Q[2:0], 1'b0}; // Clear bit in quotient
                        end
                        count <= count - 1;
                    end else begin
                        remainder <= A;
                        quotient <= Q;
                        done <= 1; // Indicate done
                        state <= 0; // Reset state
                    end
                end
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design a packet filtering module for a basic firewall. The module should take a 16-bit input packet and a 4-bit filter mask. The output should indicate whether the packet is allowed (1) or blocked (0). The packet is allowed if the result of the bitwise AND operation between the packet and the mask is equal to a predefined allowed value, which is also a 16-bit value. If the condition is met, the output should be high; otherwise, it should be low.
code:
module packet_filter (
    input [15:0] packet,
    input [3:0] filter_mask,
    output reg allowed
);

    always @(*) begin
        // Apply the filter mask to the packet
        if ((packet & {4'b0000, filter_mask}) == ALLOWED_VALUE) begin
            allowed = 1'b1; // Packet is allowed
        end else begin
            allowed = 1'b0; // Packet is blocked
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design a Bluetooth module controller that manages the connection state of a device. The controller should have an input signal that indicates whether to connect or disconnect from a device. When connecting, the state should transition to 'connected' after two clock cycles. When disconnecting, it should transition to 'disconnected' immediately. The output should indicate the current state: 0 for 'disconnected' and 1 for 'connected'.
code:
module bluetooth_controller(  
    input wire clk,  
    input wire rst,  
    input wire connect,  
    output reg state  
);  
    reg [1:0] count; // Counter for connection delay  

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin  
        if (rst) begin  
            state <= 0; // 'disconnected'  
            count <= 0;  
        end else begin  
            if (connect && state == 0) begin  
                count <= count + 1;  
                if (count == 2) begin  
                    state <= 1; // 'connected'  
                    count <= 0;  
                end  
            end else if (!connect) begin  
                state <= 0; // 'disconnected'  
                count <= 0;  
            end  
        end  
    end  
endmodule

description: Design an EEPROM cell with a single bit storage capability. The EEPROM cell should have inputs for data (D), write enable (WE), read enable (RE), and an output for the stored data (Q). Design a fixed-priority arbiter in Verilog that controls access to a shared resource for 5 requestors. The arbiter should grant access to the highest priority requestor that asserts its request signal. The output will be a grant signal indicating which requestor has been granted access. module fixed_priority_arbiter (
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst,
    input wire [4:0] request,
    output reg [4:0] grant
);
    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            grant <= 5'b00000;
        end else begin
            case (1'b1)  // Check for the highest priority request
                request[0]: grant <= 5'b00001;  // Grant to requestor 0
                request[1]: grant <= 5'b00010;  // Grant to requestor 1
                request[2]: grant <= 5'b00100;  // Grant to requestor 2
                request[3]: grant <= 5'b01000;  // Grant to requestor 3
                request[4]: grant <= 5'b10000;  // Grant to requestor 4
                default: grant <= 5'b00000;     // No grant
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

A 4-bit parallel-in serial-out (PISO) shift register that allows parallel data input and outputs the data serially. The register should have a clock and a shift control signal. When the shift control is high, the register outputs one bit of data at a time on each clock edge.

    input shift,
    input load,
    input [3:0] parallel_data,
    output reg serial_out
);

description: Design a 2-channel DMA controller that can transfer data from a source address to a destination address. The DMA controller should have two channels, allowing it to operate on two separate transfers simultaneously. The controller should have the following inputs: a clock signal (clk), a reset signal (rst), channel select (sel), source address (src_addr), destination address (dst_addr), and start signal (start). The outputs should indicate when data is being transferred (transfer_active) and which channel is currently active (active_channel).
code:
module dma_controller(
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst,
    input wire sel, // channel select: 0 for channel 0, 1 for channel 1
    input wire [31:0] src_addr,
    input wire [31:0] dst_addr,
    input wire start,
    output reg transfer_active,
    output reg [1:0] active_channel
);
    
    reg [1:0] state; // 00: idle, 01: transfer channel 0, 10: transfer channel 1

    always @(posedge clk or posedge rst) begin
        if (rst) begin
            state <= 2'b00; // reset state
            transfer_active <= 0;
            active_channel <= 2'b00;
        end else begin
            case (state)
                2'b00: begin // idle state
                    if (start) begin
                        state <= (sel) ? 2'b10 : 2'b01; // select channel
                        transfer_active <= 1;
                        active_channel <= (sel) ? 2'b10 : 2'b01;
                    end
                end
                2'b01: begin // transferring channel 0
                    // Code to perform data transfer (omitted for simplicity)
                    state <= 2'b00; // go back to idle after transfer
                    transfer_active <= 0;
                end
                2'b10: begin // transferring channel 1
                    // Code to perform data transfer (omitted for simplicity)
                    state <= 2'b00; // go back to idle after transfer
                    transfer_active <= 0;
                end
            endcase
        end
    end
endmodule

description: Design a 4-bit Parallel-in Serial-out (PISO) shift register with an enable signal to load data and a clock signal to shift out the data serially. The module should also include a reset signal to clear the register.
code:
module piso_shift_register (
    input wire clk,
    input wire reset,
    input wire load,
    input wire [3:0] data_in,
    output reg serial_out
);
    reg [3:0] shift_reg;
    reg [2:0] count; // to keep track of bits shifted out

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            shift_reg <= 4'b0000;
            count <= 3'b000;
            serial_out <= 1'b0;
        end else if (load) begin
            shift_reg <= data_in;
            count <= 3'b100; // Load the data and set count to 4 (3 bits for counting down)
        end else if (count > 0) begin
            serial_out <= shift_reg[3]; // Output the MSB
            shift_reg <= {shift_reg[2:0], 1'b0}; // Shift left
            count <= count - 1; // Decrease count
        end
    end
endmodule

module switching_regulator (
    input wire clk,
    input wire rst,
    input wire [7:0] desired_voltage,    // Desired output voltage
    input wire [7:0] measured_voltage,    // Measured output voltage
    output reg [7:0] duty_cycle           // PWM duty cycle
);

        if (rst) begin
            duty_cycle <= 8'b0;
        end else begin
            error <= desired_voltage - measured_voltage;
            if (error > 8'b0) begin
                duty_cycle <= duty_cycle + (error >> 1);  // Increase duty cycle based on error

    end
endmodule

- `disconnect`: transitions from CONNECTED or CONNECTING to DISCONNECTED.
- `reset`: resets the state machine to IDLE.

- 00: IDLE
- 01: CONNECTING
- 10: CONNECTED
- 11: DISCONNECTED

    input wire reset,
    input wire start_connection,
    input wire confirm_connection,
    input wire disconnect,
    output reg [1:0] state
);

    parameter IDLE = 2'b00, CONNECTING = 2'b01, CONNECTED = 2'b10, DISCONNECTED = 2'b11;

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin
        if (reset) begin
            state <= IDLE;
        end else begin
            case (state)
                IDLE: begin
                    if (start_connection) state <= CONNECTING;
                end
                CONNECTING: begin
                    if (confirm_connection) state <= CONNECTED;
                    else if (disconnect) state <= DISCONNECTED;

                CONNECTED: begin
                    if (disconnect) state <= DISCONNECTED;

    input wire reset,  
    input wire enable,  
    input wire [7:0] data_in,  
    output reg tx

    reg [3:0] bit_counter;  
    reg [9:0] shift_reg;  // 1 start bit + 8 data bits + 1 stop bit  

    parameter IDLE = 4'b0000, START = 4'b0001, DATA = 4'b0010, STOP = 4'b0011;  

    always @(posedge clk or posedge reset) begin  
        if (reset) begin  
            state <= IDLE;  
            tx <= 1;  // Idle state is high  
        end else begin  
            case (state)  
                IDLE: begin  
                    if (enable) begin  
                        shift_reg <= {1'b1, data_in, 1'b0};  // Stop bit + data + start bit  
                        bit_counter <= 0;  
                        state <= START;  
                    end  
                end  
                START: begin  
                    tx <= 0;  // Start bit  
                    state <= DATA;  
                end  
                DATA: begin  
                    tx <= shift_reg[bit_counter + 1];  // Transmit next data bit  
                    bit_counter <= bit_counter + 1;  
                    if (bit_counter == 8) begin  
                        state <= STOP;  
                    end  
                end  
                STOP: begin  
                    tx <= 1;  // Stop bit  
                    state <= IDLE;  
                end  
            endcase  
        end  
    end

    output reg [15:0] ALU_result
);
    always @(*) begin

            4'b0000: ALU_result = A + B;             // Addition

            4'b0011: ALU_result = A | B;             // Bitwise OR

            4'b0101: ALU_result = A << 1;            // Logical Shift Left
            4'b0110: ALU_result = A >> 1;            // Logical Shift Right
            4'b0111: ALU_result = (A < B) ? 16'b1 : 16'b0; // Comparison
            default: ALU_result = 16'b0000000000000000; // Default case
        endcase
    end
endmodule

description: Design a fixed-priority arbiter that grants access to one of four requests based on fixed priority. The arbiter should grant access to the highest priority request that is active on the rising edge of the clock.
code:
module fixed_priority_arbiter(
    input clk,
    input [3:0] req,
    output reg [3:0] grant
);
    always @(posedge clk) begin
        grant <= 4'b0000; // Reset grant
        if (req[0]) grant <= 4'b0001; // Grant req[0]
        else if (req[1]) grant <= 4'b0010; // Grant req[1]
        else if (req[2]) grant <= 4'b0100; // Grant req[2]

module vco (

    input wire enable,
    input wire [7:0] V_control,  // 8-bit control voltage input
    output reg freq_out
);

        if (enable) begin
            // The frequency output is determined by the control voltage

            if (counter >= (255 - V_control)) begin

    input [7:0] sensor_reading,

);

                end
                2'b10: begin // Move Down

                    pos_x <= pos_x + 1;

        end
    end
